messages.subject: question about plotLodProfile
parts:
I am using the R/QTL for my research.

One problem I am facing is that when I using the plotLodProfile function, it can only give me the plot on the chromosome(s) that QTL identified. How can I include all the chromosomes in the plot (including those no QTL was identified)?

Also, is it possbile to add the LOD threshold line to the above plot?

Thank you!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: question about plotLodProfile
parts:
On Monday, August 18, 2014 12:11:57 PM UTC-5, can wrote:
I am using the R/QTL for my research.

One problem I am facing is that when I using the plotLodProfile function, it can only give me the plot on the chromosome(s) that QTL identified. How can I include all the chromosomes in the plot (including those no QTL was identified)?

You can use the argument showallchr=TRUE.  Here's an example.

  data(fake.bc)
  fake.bc <- calc.genoprob(fake.bc, step=1)
  qtl <- makeqtl(fake.bc, chr=c(2,5), pos=c(32.5, 17.5),
                 what="prob")
  rqtl <- refineqtl(fake.bc, qtl=qtl, method="hk",
                    keeplodprofile=TRUE)
  plotLodProfile(rqtl, showallchr=TRUE)
Also, is it possbile to add the LOD threshold line to the above plot?

Use something like abline(h=3.5)

karl

Thanks for that Karl,
My (inelegant) solution to this has so far been to: 
1. extract the stepwise lod profiles lp_phenotype1 <-attr(stepwise_phenotype1,"lodprofile")
2.plot a scanone plot with col="white" (adjusting the y limits if necessary)
3.use the lines function to add the stepwise lod profiles.
